name: DaVinci White Flash Transition
use_when: A short-form cut, B-roll insert, or energetic section change needs a quick flash transition.
The editor wants a simple Resolve-native transition that can be built manually or with the built-in brightness flash.
A visual beat needs more energy than a straight cut but less complexity than a full motion transition.
avoid_when: The transition would distract from speech, face, proof, or emotional content.
Repeated flashes would become visually tiring or accessibility-hostile.
The built-in transition glitches and the manual version has not been checked.

timeline_pattern.manual_rule: A solid white generator or compound clip can be keyframed with opacity around the cut.
timeline_pattern.builtin_rule: Resolve's white/brightness flash transition can work well, but check for bugs or unwanted fade behavior.
timeline_pattern.reuse_rule: Save a checked flash as a preset or Power Bin item for consistent use.

motion.rule: Flash should be brief and tied to a cut, beat, or B-roll entry.

sound.rule: Add a soft hit or whoosh only when the flash needs a sound accent; keep dialogue clear.

captions.rule: Avoid flashing over captions that must be read at that exact moment.

color.rule: Use full white only briefly; do not wash out the next shot long enough to hide the subject.

implementation.ffmpeg: Overlay a white color source with alpha keyframes around the cut or use a short xfade-style white flash segment.
implementation.remotion: Add a white full-screen layer with opacity keyframes around the transition frame.
implementation.blender: Use a white overlay plane or compositor color mix with keyframed factor around the cut.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use a white flash transition or a white overlay with keyframed opacity.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Dip to White, an adjustment layer/white matte opacity flash, or a saved flash preset.

common_mistakes: Letting the flash hide a caption or important face/action moment.
Trusting the built-in transition without checking for bugs or unwanted timing.
Making the flash too long for a fast short-form edit.
qc: Does the flash land on an intentional cut or beat?
Is the flash short enough to avoid hiding the next shot?
Does it avoid covering captions that need to be read?
Is repeated flash use limited enough to avoid fatigue?
Does the manual or built-in version render cleanly?
